comparable.host_disk: Amazon Elastic Block Store, non-rotational (kernel flag), nvme, ext4

exactly-once.text:
# Kafka Connect S3 sink, Lenses Stream Reactor kafka-connect-aws-s3 12.1.2, profile `exactly-once`, for the
# archive comparison (#746). Every setting names its page: the connector's documentation
# https://docs.lenses.io/latest/connectors/kafka-connectors/sinks/aws-s3 (the "KCQL", "Flush options",
# "Compression", "Authentication" and "Configuration" sections) as published for 12.x.
#
# The worker's own settings are worker.properties beside this file; the runtime is the Connect of
# apache/kafka 4.3.2, standalone (one worker, no internal topics), the JVM heap capped at -Xmx1g by the
# compose file.
#
# telemetry: Kafka Connect and the connector have no usage reporting or update check; the connector's JMX
# metrics are not exported anywhere.
#
# commit rule: with connect.s3.exactly.once.enable (the documented default) the consumer offset advances only
# after the object is at its final key and the `.indexes/` entry is updated ("Restart behavior").
name=archive-bench
connector.class=io.lenses.streamreactor.connect.aws.s3.sink.S3SinkConnector
# "Configuration": one task per partition. The consumer group is connect-archive-bench.
tasks.max=3
topics=bench

# "KCQL" and "Flush options" (#744 rule 15: about 32 MiB or 60 s per object, whichever first; the record
# count is high). `flush.size` is bytes and `flush.interval` is seconds; the connector measures flush.size on the
# staged file, so the object's size is reported as measured, not assumed to be 32 MiB. STOREAS `JSON` writes one
# JSON object per line, as the converter in worker.properties parsed it.
connect.s3.kcql=INSERT INTO bench:connect SELECT * FROM bench STOREAS `JSON` PROPERTIES('flush.size'=33554432,'flush.interval'=60,'flush.count'=100000000)

# "Compression": gzip at the connector's default level (connect.s3.compression.level is left unset).
connect.s3.compression.codec=GZIP

# "Authentication" (Credentials mode: the lab MinIO's keys) and the lab store's endpoint, path-style.
connect.s3.aws.auth.mode=Credentials
connect.s3.aws.access.key=minioadmin
connect.s3.aws.secret.key=minioadmin
connect.s3.aws.region=us-east-1
connect.s3.custom.endpoint=http://minio:9000
connect.s3.path.style.access=true

# "Restart behavior": exactly-once is the default; stated here so the profile is visible in the CSV's config hash.
connect.s3.exactly.once.enable=true

# "Local staging": records are appended to a file on the worker's disk (the tool's data volume) before a flush.
connect.s3.local.tmp.directory=/data/tmp

acks.text:
# Vector 0.61.0, profile `acks`, for the archive comparison (#746). Each setting names
# its page under https://vector.dev/docs/ (as published for 0.61).
#
# telemetry: Vector has no usage reporting; its API server is off
# (reference/api/: `api.enabled`, default false, stated here).

# reference/configuration/global-options/#data_dir: checkpoints and buffers on the tool's own volume.
data_dir: /var/lib/vector

api:
  enabled: false

sources:
  topic:
    # reference/configuration/sources/kafka/: one topic, a consumer group of its own, from the start.
    type: kafka
    bootstrap_servers: kafka:9092
    group_id: vector-bench
    topics: [bench]
    auto_offset_reset: earliest
    # sources/kafka/#decoding: the record's value is the event's `message`, byte for byte.
    decoding:
      codec: bytes
    # sources/kafka/#acknowledgements is deprecated in favour of the sink's setting below: the
    # consumer group's offset moves only after the sink has delivered the event.

sinks:
  s3:
    # reference/configuration/sinks/aws_s3/
    type: aws_s3
    inputs: [topic]
    bucket: bench
    key_prefix: "vector/%Y/%m/%d/"
    region: us-east-1
    # sinks/aws_s3/#endpoint: the lab MinIO (the S3 tap in crash cells).
    endpoint: http://minio:9000
    force_path_style: true
    # #744 rule 15: one JSON line per record (the Kafka value, newline-delimited), gzip at its default level.
    encoding:
      codec: raw_message
    framing:
      method: newline_delimited
    compression: gzip
    # #744 rule 15: about 32 MiB or 60 s per object.
    batch:
      max_bytes: 33554432
      timeout_secs: 60
    # sinks/aws_s3/#request.concurrency: the default.
    request:
      concurrency: adaptive
    # reference/end-to-end-acknowledgements/: the Kafka offset advances only after this sink
    # has delivered the event.
    acknowledgements:
      enabled: true
    # reference/configuration/sinks/aws_s3/#buffer: a memory buffer that blocks
    # when full, so nothing is acknowledged before delivery.
    buffer:
      type: memory
      max_events: 10000
      when_full: block
    # Credentials come from AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in the
    # container's environment (sinks/aws_s3/#auth, the default chain).

disk-buffer.text:
# Vector 0.61.0, profile `disk-buffer`, for the archive comparison (#746). Each setting names
# its page under https://vector.dev/docs/ (as published for 0.61). It differs from `acks` in the buffer only.
#
# telemetry: Vector has no usage reporting; its API server is off
# (reference/api/: `api.enabled`, default false, stated here).

# reference/configuration/global-options/#data_dir: checkpoints and buffers on the tool's own volume.
data_dir: /var/lib/vector

api:
  enabled: false

sources:
  topic:
    # reference/configuration/sources/kafka/: one topic, a consumer group of its own, from the start.
    type: kafka
    bootstrap_servers: kafka:9092
    group_id: vector-bench
    topics: [bench]
    auto_offset_reset: earliest
    # sources/kafka/#decoding: the record's value is the event's `message`, byte for byte.
    decoding:
      codec: bytes

sinks:
  s3:
    # reference/configuration/sinks/aws_s3/
    type: aws_s3
    inputs: [topic]
    bucket: bench
    key_prefix: "vector/%Y/%m/%d/"
    region: us-east-1
    # sinks/aws_s3/#endpoint: the lab MinIO (the S3 tap in crash cells).
    endpoint: http://minio:9000
    force_path_style: true
    # #744 rule 15: one JSON line per record (the Kafka value, newline-delimited), gzip at its default level.
    encoding:
      codec: raw_message
    framing:
      method: newline_delimited
    compression: gzip
    # #744 rule 15: about 32 MiB or 60 s per object.
    batch:
      max_bytes: 33554432
      timeout_secs: 60
    # sinks/aws_s3/#request.concurrency: the default.
    request:
      concurrency: adaptive
    # reference/end-to-end-acknowledgements/
    acknowledgements:
      enabled: true
    # reference/configuration/sinks/aws_s3/#buffer: a disk buffer; with it an event is
    # acknowledged once it is in the buffer, which is synced every 500 ms
    # (reference/end-to-end-acknowledgements/). The documented durability trade.
    buffer:
      type: disk
      max_size: 1073741824
      when_full: block
    # Credentials come from AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in the
    # container's environment (sinks/aws_s3/#auth, the default chain).

strong.text:
# VTOP, profile `strong` (the default commit rule), for the archive comparison (#746).
# Every setting names the page it comes from: docs/configure/reference.md (the
# reference for every config.yaml key), docs/install/kafka.md and examples/config.yaml
# at the commit under test.
#
# telemetry: VTOP has no usage reporting; OpenTelemetry export runs only when an
# OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*ENDPOINT is set, and the compose file sets
# OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true (crates/vtop-observe/src/otel/settings.rs).
#
# commit rule: the Kafka offset is committed only after the batch is VERIFIED
# (docs/install/kafka.md, `enable_auto_commit` must be false).

engine:
  name: archive-bench
  tenant: bench
  # docs/configure/reference.md "engine.state_store": SQLite on the tool's own data volume,
  # the same volume class as every other tool's state.
  state_store: "sqlite:///data/state/vtop-state.db"
  work_dir: /data/work
  work_retention_seconds: 86400
  work_max_bytes: 10737418240
  log_level: INFO

batching:
  # #744 rule 15: about 32 MiB or 60 s per object, whichever first; records unbounded.
  # docs/configure/reference.md "batching.max_bytes", "batching.max_batch_age_seconds".
  max_records: 100000000
  max_bytes: 33554432
  max_batch_age_seconds: 60
  # The shipped default (examples/config.yaml "max_concurrent_batches").
  max_concurrent_batches: 8

compression:
  # #744 rule 15: gzip at the tool's documented default level (examples/config.yaml
  # "compression": the code default is gzip level 6).
  type: gzip
  level: 6

sources:
  kafka:
    # docs/configure/reference.md "sources.kafka": one topic, a group of its own, from the start.
    enabled: true
    bootstrap_servers:
      - kafka:9092
    consumer_group: vtop-bench
    topic_include_regex: "^bench$"
    auto_offset_reset: earliest
    # Must be false: offsets commit only after VERIFIED (the commit rule).
    enable_auto_commit: false

upload:
  # docs/configure/reference.md "upload": the native S3 backend against the lab MinIO.
  # In crash and fault cells `minio` resolves to the S3 tap, which forwards to the store.
  backend: s3_native
  bucket: bench
  prefix: "vtop/"
  endpoint_url: http://minio:9000
  region: us-east-1
  force_path_style: true
  # The lab store is plaintext (examples/config.yaml "verify_tls": the explicit lab opt-out).
  verify_tls: false
  # The lab creates the bucket before any tool starts (the harness's `mc mb`), so no tool makes a bucket PUT:
  # the S3 tap counts every PUT, and a bucket PUT answered 409 would be the Nth request that a K2 trigger
  # waits for and never sees succeed (docs/configure/reference.md "upload.create_bucket", default false).
  create_bucket: false
  # The default: VERIFIED needs a digest derived from stored content.
  require_strong_verification: true

partitioning:
  template: "source={source}/format={format}/"

verify-off.text:
# VTOP, profile `verify-off` (non-default, labelled), for the archive comparison (#746).
# It isolates what verification costs: the same configuration as `strong` with the verification floor lowered
# (`upload.require_strong_verification: false`, which docs/configure/reference.md says "accepts same-size
# corruption") and the checksum algorithm `none` (docs/configure/streams.md: "`none` checks size only"; refused
# while the floor is strong). It is run in `drain` and `live` only, never in a crash or fault cell, where it would
# measure a deliberate weakening (#746), and it is never a second orange bar.
#
# telemetry: as `strong`; the compose file sets OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true.

engine:
  name: archive-bench
  tenant: bench
  state_store: "sqlite:///data/state/vtop-state.db"
  work_dir: /data/work
  work_retention_seconds: 86400
  work_max_bytes: 10737418240
  log_level: INFO

batching:
  max_records: 100000000
  max_bytes: 33554432
  max_batch_age_seconds: 60
  max_concurrent_batches: 8

compression:
  type: gzip
  level: 6

# docs/configure/reference.md "checksum.algorithm": `none` verifies size only.
checksum:
  algorithm: none

sources:
  kafka:
    enabled: true
    bootstrap_servers:
      - kafka:9092
    consumer_group: vtop-bench
    topic_include_regex: "^bench$"
    auto_offset_reset: earliest
    enable_auto_commit: false

upload:
  backend: s3_native
  bucket: bench
  prefix: "vtop/"
  endpoint_url: http://minio:9000
  region: us-east-1
  force_path_style: true
  verify_tls: false
  # The lab creates the bucket before any tool starts (the harness's `mc mb`), so no tool makes a bucket PUT:
  # the S3 tap counts every PUT, and a bucket PUT answered 409 would be the Nth request that a K2 trigger
  # waits for and never sees succeed (docs/configure/reference.md "upload.create_bucket", default false).
  create_bucket: false
  # The deliberate weakening this profile exists to measure.
  require_strong_verification: false

partitioning:
  template: "source={source}/format={format}/"

deviations: The record is one JSON object per Kafka value. VTOP and Vector store the value as it came, newline-framed; Connect (Lenses) parses it with its JSON converter and writes it again, so its bytes may differ and its content may not. The smoke counts byte-exact and JSON-equal records separately; the checker reads the id token in either form, and MiB/s is of source bytes (the value as produced), so the framing does not change it (rule 15).

Object size is set by each tool's documented threshold nearest to 'about 32 MiB uncompressed or 60 s': VTOP `batching.max_bytes` and Vector `batch.max_bytes` count uncompressed payload; Connect (Lenses) `flush.size` counts the staged file. The measured object sizes (p50 and p99) are reported.

Connect's `.temp-upload/` objects (the staging step of its exactly-once commit) and `.indexes/` entries (its commit-chain bookkeeping) are counted as orphan objects and listed by name, as #746 specifies; the `.indexes/` entries are permanent by design, so Connect's orphan count has a floor.

Connect's offsets are committed by its worker at `offset.flush.interval.ms` (the 60 s default), so its time to source-committed includes up to that interval; Vector commits every 5 s by default; VTOP after VERIFIED.

The producer is `kafka-console-producer.sh` (acks=all, linger.ms=5) fed by the seeded generator; the produce time of a record is the generator's write time, up to 5 ms before the send. Partitions come from the key's murmur2 hash, the broker's default partitioner, checked against the partition end offsets before a tool starts.

Time to store-visible (MinIO's LastModified, ms), time to source-committed (the broker's stamp on the group's offset commit) and the producer's write time share the Docker VM's clock; the window start and the kill times are the harness host's clock, which is the same clock on a Linux host.
Connect runs in standalone mode (one worker, no internal topics); its sink tasks' offsets are committed to the consumer group, as in distributed mode (#746 open question 2).

plan._comment: The hosted plan's kills at a seeded time (K3) and the corrupted read-back cell: one hosted job, about 3 hours projected, with its own smoke.

telemetry.vector: no usage reporting; API server off (api.enabled: false)
telemetry.vtop: no usage reporting; OpenTelemetry export off (OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true, no endpoint set)
